newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal eyes 30 pct of net for buy-back.
newsitem.headline: Universal eyes 30 pct of net for buy-back.

text.p: Polish trader Universal SA plans to allot not more than 30 percent of its 1996 profit of 23 million zlotys to its scheme to buy back and retire shares, the firm's spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"Definitely it (the buy-back allotment), will not be more than 30 percent of net profit" Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters.

She said the buy-back and the planned allotment of 10 percent of the firm's shares for American Depositary Receipts would lower the liquidity of the firm's shares on the Warsaw bourse and positively affect their market price. @

Universal said on Tuesday it did not plan to pay a dividend for 1996 because last year's profits would go to the buy-back scheme, reserve capital, bonuses for supervisory board members and a fund for employees.
Szostek said that in the next few days management would decide on the detailed breakdown of the profit's allocation and from whom shares would be bought.
She said shareholders would vote on the decisions in the first 10 days of April. @
Shares of Universal, which currently has 23,100,510 shares outstanding and did not pay a 1995 dividend, closed at 12.6 zlotys on Wednesday.
